directAnswer: To fix Bluetooth issues in Windows, ensure Bluetooth is enabled in settings and update your Bluetooth drivers through Device Manager.
summary: This guide provides steps to troubleshoot and resolve Bluetooth connectivity issues in Windows.

sections.heading: Check Bluetooth Status
sections.body: First, verify that Bluetooth is enabled on your device. Go to Settings > Devices > Bluetooth & other devices and ensure the Bluetooth toggle is turned on.

sections.heading: Update Bluetooth Drivers
sections.body: Outdated drivers can cause connectivity issues. Open Device Manager, find Bluetooth, right-click on your Bluetooth device, and select 'Update driver'.

sections.heading: Run Bluetooth Troubleshooter
sections.body: Windows has a built-in troubleshooter for Bluetooth. Go to Settings > Update & Security > Troubleshoot > Additional troubleshooters, and select 'Bluetooth'.

steps.title: Enable Bluetooth
steps.detail: Go to Settings > Devices > Bluetooth & other devices and toggle Bluetooth on.

steps.title: Update Drivers
steps.detail: Open Device Manager, locate Bluetooth, right-click your device, and choose 'Update driver'.

steps.title: Run Troubleshooter
steps.detail: Navigate to Settings > Update & Security > Troubleshoot > Additional troubleshooters and select 'Bluetooth' to run the troubleshooter.

faqs.question: What should I do if my Bluetooth device is not recognized?
faqs.answer: Ensure the device is in pairing mode and within range. Restart both your PC and the Bluetooth device.

faqs.question: How can I remove a Bluetooth device?
faqs.answer: Go to Settings > Devices > Bluetooth & other devices, select the device you want to remove, and click 'Remove device'.

faqs.question: Why does my Bluetooth keep disconnecting?
faqs.answer: This could be due to interference, low battery on the Bluetooth device, or outdated drivers. Try updating drivers and ensuring no other devices are causing interference.

caveats: Bluetooth functionality may vary based on hardware and Windows version.
